findings.title: Lifecycle rejection bypasses the sticky failure latch
findings.requirement: round66 provenance contract item 6: identity/event/read/injection/end validation failure must mark failure, preserve evidence and prohibit successful END/retry.
findings.observation: begin_fault/end_fault_injection/check call _require_live before their try/_current failure recording. A _plan_binding or allocation-byte drift refusal therefore neither sets _failure nor appends its failure observation.
findings.static_counterexample: Start from healthy begun/ended owner below fixed deadline; change plan[attempt] from 1 to 2; check rejects at 1119->907 before _remember_failure; restore attempt to 1; finish without caller failure invokes _current successfully and reaches wall_pass=True with the already valid BEGIN/END. The analogous restored allocation-byte/process-identity observation follows the same path. This is a source-control-flow proof; no execution or new pytest run was performed.
findings.impact: An observed ownership/provenance discontinuity can be erased by restoring values, allowing software wall success. Current lifecycle cases inject caller failure at test line1095 and do not check the failure latch after restoration.
findings.action: Report to ROOT; obtain next gpt-6-astra plan before product/test repair.
